descriptions.tumor_skin_epithelial_bcc: Aggregates, cords, and lobules of intensely basophilic basaloid epithelial cells invade the dermis, classically demonstrating prominent peripheral nuclear palisading at the epithelial-stromal interface. The neoplastic cells display high nucleocytoplasmic ratios with scant cytoplasm, containing crowded, hyperchromatic, round-to-elongated nuclei with dark chromatin and scattered apoptotic bodies. Distinctive peritumoral retraction clefts frequently separate the deeply hematoxylin-stained tumor islands from the surrounding altered, loose or fibromyxoid eosinophilic stroma.
descriptions.tumor_skin_epithelial_sqcc: Infiltrative nests, cords, and irregular sheets of atypical squamous epithelial cells invade the dermis, often surrounded by a desmoplastic and chronic inflammatory stroma. Neoplastic cells display abundant glassy eosinophilic cytoplasm with distinct intercellular bridges, surrounding enlarged, pleomorphic, hyperchromatic nuclei with coarse chromatin, prominent nucleoli, and brisk mitotic activity. Characteristic squamous differentiation manifests as concentric, intensely eosinophilic keratin pearls and scattered dyskeratotic cells contrasting sharply against the hypercellular, basophilic malignant parenchyma.
descriptions.tumor_skin_melanoma_melanoma: Cutaneous melanoma displays an infiltrative and poorly circumscribed architecture composed of irregular sheets, discohesive nests, or pagetoid single-cell scatter of atypical melanocytes within the epidermis and dermis. The tumor cells exhibit marked pleomorphism, adopting epithelioid, spindle, or plasmacytoid morphologies with enlarged, vesicular or hyperchromatic nuclei, irregular nuclear membranes, and characteristically prominent, macronucleoli (often cherry-red). The cytoplasm is variable and amphophilic to eosinophilic, frequently harboring fine or coarse dusty-brown melanin pigment, alongside brisk mitotic activity with atypical figures and associated melanophages on H&E staining.
descriptions.tumor_skin_naevus_naevus: Well-circumscribed nests, cords, or cohesive sheets of uniform melanocytes (nevus cells) are arranged at the dermo-epidermal junction, within the dermis, or both, often surrounded by a collagenous stroma. The cells exhibit round to oval, monomorphic nuclei with smooth contours, finely dispersed chromatin, inconspicuous nucleoli, and an absence of significant atypia or mitotic figures. The cytoplasm is moderate and pale eosinophilic to amphophilic, frequently harboring fine, granular golden-brown melanin pigment in superficial layers and demonstrating classic maturation into smaller, neurotized-appearing cells deeper in the dermis.
descriptions.nontumor_skin_epidermis_epidermis: Normal epidermis displays an organized stratified squamous keratinized epithelium arranged in distinct maturational layers, transitioning from a basal layer anchored along undulating rete ridges to superficial squames. Basal keratinocytes contain uniform, hyperchromatic, round-to-oval nuclei, while the overlying stratum spinosum exhibits cohesive polyhedral cells with distinct intercellular bridges and moderate eosinophilic cytoplasm. The superficial aspect demonstrates a stratum granulosum filled with coarse basophilic keratohyalin granules, capped by a lamellated, anucleate, brightly eosinophilic stratum corneum with a characteristic basket-weave texture.
descriptions.nontumor_skin_dermis_dermis: Normal dermis is characterized by an extracellular matrix dominated by dense, wavy, and interwoven bundles of coarse, brightly eosinophilic collagen fibers. Sparsely scattered between these collagenous bands are quiescent spindle-shaped fibroblasts possessing slender, elongated, hyperchromatic nuclei with tapered ends and inconspicuous cytoplasm. The architecture displays a distinctly fibrillar and hypocellular texture, interspersed with pale interstitial clefts and occasional small, thin-walled capillary vessels without mitotic activity or cytologic atypia.
descriptions.nontumor_skin_subcutis_subcutis: The subcutaneous tissue is predominantly composed of expansive lobules of mature, unilocular adipocytes partitioned by delicate, pale eosinophilic fibrovascular septa. The tissue exhibits a classic optically clear honeycomb or chicken-wire architecture resulting from standard histologic lipid dissolution during processing. Individual adipocytes possess large, vacant cytoplasmic spaces defined by crisp, thin cell membranes with small, flattened, hyperchromatic nuclei compressed eccentrically along the periphery. The overall texture is light and mesh-like, containing slender interlobular collagen strands and small, normal-caliber capillaries without evidence of cellular atypia or necrosis.
descriptions.nontumor_skin_hairfollicle_hairfollicle: Normal cutaneous hair follicles present as rounded to elongated multi-layered epithelial structures within the dermis or subcutis, organized concentrically into an outer root sheath, an inner root sheath, and a central densely compact, brightly eosinophilic or pigmented hair shaft. The outer root sheath consists of pale to clear glycogenated squamous cells with peripheral palisading of uniform, oval basaloid nuclei, while the inner layers display coarse, intensely eosinophilic trichohyalin granules and specialized compact keratinization. The entire follicular unit is circumscribed by a distinct hyaline basement membrane and a delicate, concentric fibrous connective tissue sheath.
descriptions.nontumor_skin_sebaceousglands_sebaceousg: Benign sebaceous glands present as well-circumscribed, multilobular acini within the dermis, characterized by large, polygonal sebocytes with distinct cell boundaries and pale, bubbly, lipid-rich cytoplasm with a finely vacuolated or foamy texture. Centrally located, small, round to indented nuclei are suspended within the clear cytoplasmic matrix of mature sebocytes. The periphery of each lobule is lined by a distinct, thin rim of small, hyperchromatic, basophilic basaloid germinative cells.
descriptions.nontumor_skin_sweatglands_sweatglands: In cross-section, non-neoplastic sweat glands appear as distinct lobular clusters of round to oval coiled tubules and ducts embedded within dermal or subcutaneous fibrofatty stroma. The secretory coils consist of pale, amphophilic-to-eosinophilic cuboidal or columnar epithelial cells with uniform, round, basally situated nuclei, surrounded by an outer layer of flattened myoepithelial cells. Associated excretory ducts display a distinctive double layer of compact, hyperchromatic cuboidal cells featuring dense basophilic nuclei and a sharply delineated eosinophilic cuticular border along open, circular lumina.
descriptions.nontumor_skin_vessel_vessel: Dermal and subcutaneous blood vessels are characterized by round, oval, or branching lumina lined by a single layer of flattened endothelial cells, frequently containing bright orange-red to intensely eosinophilic erythrocytes within the vascular spaces. Endothelial nuclei are attenuated, spindle-shaped, or ovoid with bland, dark basophilic chromatin, resting on a delicate basement membrane. Depending on vessel caliber, the walls display concentric, fibrillar pink smooth muscle layers and adventitial connective tissue with elongated cigar-shaped nuclei, blending seamlessly into the surrounding collagenous stroma without nuclear pleomorphism or malignant architectural distortion.
descriptions.nontumor_skin_nerves_nerves: Cutaneous peripheral nerves appear as discrete, well-circumscribed round-to-oval fascicular bundles enveloped by a thin, delicate perineurium within the dermis or subcutaneous tissue. They display a characteristic pale eosinophilic, finely fibrillar, or subtly vacuolated background of neurofilaments and Schwann cell cytoplasm, presenting a looser texture than the dense, coarse surrounding collagen. Embedded Schwann cell and endoneurial nuclei are typically elongated, slender, wavy, or tapered with bland, condensed chromatin and no significant cytologic atypia.
descriptions.nontumor_skin_muscle_skeletal: Histopathologic sections show organized, parallel fascicles of elongated, multinucleated cylindrical myofibers exhibiting deeply eosinophilic, dense cytoplasm with distinct transverse cross-striations. In cross-section, the fibers present as cohesive, polygonal units with a finely granular texture, compartmentalized by delicate fibrovascular perimysium and endomysium. Multiple uniform, flattened to oval nuclei with evenly dispersed chromatin are strictly situated peripherally beneath the sarcolemma, without atypia, hyperchromasia, or mitotic figures.
descriptions.nontumor_skin_chondraltissue_chondraltis: Mature cartilaginous tissue composed of chondrocytes arranged individually or in small isogenous clusters embedded within rounded, well-defined lacunae. The chondrocytes exhibit small, round, hyperchromatic nuclei with pale or clear cytoplasm, frequently showing artifactual shrinkage within their lacunar spaces. The surrounding extracellular matrix displays a dense, smooth to fibrillar texture with a characteristic basophilic, violaceous, or amphophilic staining that sharply demarcates it from adjacent fibroconnective perichondrium.
descriptions.nontumor_skin_elastosis_elastosis: The superficial to mid-dermis exhibits broad, band-like zones of degraded, basophilic to slate-gray elastotic material replacing normal dense eosinophilic collagen bundles, often separated from the epidermis by a narrow grenz zone. This altered dermal matrix features a coarse, clumped, tangled, or amorphous fibrillar texture characterized by thickened, fragmented, and curled degenerated elastic fibers. Cellularity is distinctly low, containing only sparse, quiescent spindle-shaped fibroblasts with small, elongated, bland nuclei devoid of cytologic atypia or mitotic activity.
descriptions.nontumor_skin_necrosis_necrosis: Histopathology reveals marked tissue architecture breakdown characterized by confluent sheets of smudgy, intensely hypereosinophilic acellular debris and preserved pale ghost-cell outlines. Resident cutaneous cells exhibit pronounced nuclear degeneration including dense pyknosis, fragmented basophilic karyorrhectic dust, and widespread karyolysis. The surrounding tissue demonstrates a granular, disorganized, and friable texture, frequently accompanied by extravasated erythrocytes, fibrin deposition, and a peripheral rim of degenerate neutrophilic infiltrate.

prompt_template: You are a pathologist writing a detailed morphological description for the class {class_name!r} (dataset: {dataset}), to be encoded by a vision-language model's text tower and compared against histopathology image patches. Cover: cell/nuclear shape, arrangement or architecture, texture, and any distinctive staining pattern. 2-4 sentences. Output only the description, no preamble, no quotes.
